description:
Retire the private memory-backed setups of the `fast_rules` suite.

## Background

Shared test support builds a memory store and executor from declarations passed as data, on top of the shared memory executor. Helpers that act on a `TestHarness` or executor they are given are scenario steps, not setups. 

Helpers to retire, from the mechanical sweep in investigation §D.6 (function names are the identity; lines at `a5aac64b1`):

- `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/example_rulesets_tests.rs`: `executor_with_sdd_example` (`:612`), `research_coverage_executor` (`:1524`).
- `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/label_strategic_tests.rs`: `strategic_executor` (`:13`).
- `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/local_rule_enforcement_tests.rs`: `executor_with_rules` (`:20`).
- `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/project_render_harness_tests.rs`: `storage_with` (`:77`), `render_executor` (`:90`).
- `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/validate_rule_runner_tests.rs`: `store_with_rules` (`:21`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each helper under "Helpers to retire" no longer exists, and the tests that called it obtain what it built from the shared fixtures.
- [hard] REQ-02: No file in `fast_rules` defines a function that constructs an `InMemoryStorage` or a memory executor; no test writes an index body or restates a value product initialisation already writes, and scenario values (for example `enforce_leases = "off"`) reach the shared constructor as declarations.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each affected test asserts what it asserted before.
title: fast_rules memory-backed tests use the shared seeding
